title: Wisdom, Peace, and the Just Judgment
english: The holy one does not speak these things from his own person, but concerning the human race having been tested by many evils and tribulation before the arrival of the Savior. After the trial, the Lord, having turned back toward us, came and gave life, having given instead of us his own soul as a ransom; so that everyone believing in him and receiving his teaching possesses eternal life. He brought up [me] from the abysses of the earth, that is, from Hades, having become there after the shedding of the body, and no one else resurrected [me] except him, to bring up those having been cast down there through their own sin.

Regarding 'You have brought me up again from the abysses of the earth' (Ps 70:21): if the abyss signifies a sinking in circumstantial matters (as it is interpreted), it follows to take it as being often raised up from there by God, always doing good (the testimony of this is the saying: 'Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and from all of them the Lord will rescue them'); but if instead of Hades the abyss is understood, it is difficult to say how someone is raised up there again; for just as there is one entrance into life and one exit from it, it is necessary that those being separated from the body also become one in Hades. Therefore, the 'again' does not pass by, but will find consolation; yet it is not passing by the divine and is not superfluous. His thought will be such: 'Having given me life by your goodness, and also having increased your righteousness upon me, you have brought me up again from the abysses of the earth, not only by having given me life and having increased your righteousness upon me, but also by bringing me up from the lower parts.'

The Psalter is a vessel of the psalm, through which he says 'I will confess to you,' bringing forth the truth thankfully, according to which no one is like God after having made bad things life-giving and having completed every following goodness. Regarding the confessing of the truth in a vessel of a psalm and in a harp, he promises to the God existing, the Holy of Israel. And 'Holy of Israel' is said as one sanctifying him; for just as if we say 'they are holy of God' we present those being sanctified by him, so we do not say 'Holy of him' without signifying what is being sanctified. And if it is not so, attend to what is said concerning Christ, who...

Wisdom was revealed to us from God, along with righteousness, sanctification, and redemption; for wisdom became for the wise, righteousness for those being justified, and sanctification and redemption for those being sanctified and redeemed. It is not only said that the Holy One of Israel is God, but also in the Parousia, the Holy One of Israel [is revealed], making manifest what the sinners [do]. The rational soul is redeemed, because Jesus gave his own soul as a ransom for it, and it is clearly a rational soul. For just as he redeemed the bodies of men by giving a body of the same essence for them, so he redeemed rational souls by placing a rational soul for them.

Regarding Psalm 71, the psalm does not pertain to the father of Rehoboam, Solomon, but to the one called spiritual, through the participation in the name; for it is interpreted with a Greek voice of peace. For who is he who says, 'Jesus, I give you my peace'? Concerning this, the theologian writes: 'For He is our peace' (Eph 2:14), and 'He preached peace to you who are far off, and peace to those who are near' (Eph 2:17), having dissolved the enmity that divided Greeks from Hebrews, as one flock and establishing one people from the nations and Jews. Thus, being shown to be peaceful through his works, he who was born according to the flesh from a virgin is from David. Indeed, it is written concerning him, 'The Book of the generation of Jesus Christ, Son of David' (Matt 1:1).

Regarding Psalm 71:2, 'To judge your people in righteousness (clearly those of the circumcision) and your poor in judgment' (Ps 72:2); for those coming to the gospel from the nations are not called poor because of a poverty of unbelief and wickedness. But if the poor of God can be the moderate in mind, according to 'Blessed are the poor in spirit' (Matt 5:3), [then He] visits them. Regarding Psalm 71:3, [He] protects the great-minded through virtue, the high-born and those called princes, to take up peace toward the people. And even if the high-born and princes turn out to be archangels and angels, the whole human race is a people toward whom they are called to bring peace, since Jesus, through the blood of the cross, made peace between those in the heavens and those on the earth, who previously were at odds on the earth because of wickedness toward those in the heavens. Since, therefore, the one crucified...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Church as the Moon
english: The Lamb of God is sacrificed, and by this the sin of the world is released, the sin of those upon the earth; peace is being made between those in the heavens and those upon the earth, joy being made in the heavens before the angels for those repenting from sin. And if Moses and the prophets are signified by mountains and hills, let them take up peace toward the people from the nations who disbelieved, knowing what they themselves had previously spoken concerning this calling. And since even among those possessing virtue, some more so and others having it less, it must be said of those possessing it more as being increased in greater measure by practice and knowledge of the truth, that they are the higher mountains compared to the lower hills. [Ps 71:4] For it is the work of him who received from God judgment and righteousness, to judge the poor of the people.

Not such are those clinging to the letter and the shadow of the law, always named poor, seeing sharply the wealth of not having possessed the spiritual law, having that which the ones from the Jews who believed have, and the apostles also are such. Toward this also he brings salvation to the sons of the penitent. Not such are those who have come from idolatry to the faith of Jesus, those who were born of them according to the superstition of the penitent. Therefore, he will not leave them remaining in many-sided error, but will save their sons having recognized [the truth]. These having been rescued and saved, in order to judge and having come to save, he humbles the one who tyrannizes all in slander, so that he might be crushed as under the feet of the saints. For toward the righteous it is said, 'And you shall tread upon the lion and the dragon,' [Ps 71:5] and toward a man (and toward every slanderer), if he were to say, 'He will turn away slander.'

The same is said to the one remaining with the anointed, what was said to him: 'You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek,' [Ps 110:4] and 'Before the moon, generations of generations, the same one established me before the age.' [Ps 89:2] It is said 'He remains with the anointed' concerning the flesh which he clothed himself with, the soul being breathed into it, being both rational and spiritual; for he remains with the anointed of righteousness because of the indivisible union. But even before the moon, which has the analogy to the sun, there exists a generation of generations, for the church is established through him and in him, composed of all the generations.

They have it from generation to generation in succession. It is presented from the cloud of the waters as the moon is the church; but not thus: Who is she, emerging like the dew, beautiful as the moon, chosen? (Ps 71:6) Just as the rain comes upon the earth bringing fertility, so the visitation of the Savior to men has become the generation of righteousness.

It must be said that the cloud signifies Israel, and the earth signifies the Gentiles. Since previously it descended upon the cloud, and then from there upon the earth. For because Israel disobeyed and did not receive the one who had come, there was a transition to the rain upon the earth, so that all the men upon it might be moistened, rather being watered from the drops to bear spiritual fruits. (Ps 71:7) In the days of the Savior's visitation, the light of practical virtue of righteousness rises, and with it the evangelical standing through the faith of Jesus among the living, and the appropriate peace, possessing a great multitude, so as to extend until the completion of the world. For this is what the reflection of the moon signifies. (Ps 71:7b)

We say that the moon signifies the church. For the moon receives light as a derivative from the sun and does not possess it from itself; so the church, being upon the earth, knows in part and has not been truly illuminated, destined one day to be according to the sun, the perfect one... [gap] ...destined not to have been truly illuminated by appearance, then this happening according to the sun, so that it may receive the perfect [light] and face to face. For by the Word, knowing in part is abolished, and the surpassing knowledge will be established. Thus the lunar condition of the church will be abolished when the sun of righteousness comes, shining like the sun, completing the church of the righteous in the kingdom of their own Father. [gap] ...in the cloud of the waters is the perfection of the bride; and the church itself, after much progress, will be according to the sun. For who is she, he says, emerging like the dew, possessing the beginning of illumination, with which the beginning will be, as the moon, approaching? For she... [gap] ...with which there will be wonder like the sun. (Ps 71:9-11a) Understandings [are] not thus: of those from the nations, the Ethiopians.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fruitfulness of the Support and the Drying of the Grass
english: Regarding those called through their existence out of impiety, falling down before the king in a manner of recognition, the Jews, who are the king's enemies, will indeed be lacking. And it also seems that the Ethiopians fall down before him; the falling down before the king, who sees the hidden things, demonstrates genuine submission.

It is also possible for the enemies of God to appear to have the sensation of repentance through the fact that they lack; for they are bowing down. Tharsis takes hold of the opportunity to spy out joys, spying out the joy of the friends of virtue and piety, if one might ever be able to hear: 'Come into the joy of your Lord' (Matt 25:21).

Those not having a contemplative gaze toward the joy, the kings who hold [their power] bring their gifts to those who are beginning. And islands are brought forward. But these are souls, possessing themselves firmly and unmovably, even when the sea stirs up a gale and a storm. To these, the Savior says: 'Dedicate yourselves, islands, to me, being renewed by the newness of the Spirit, bearing the new human being created according to God.'

Along with these kings, also the Arabs and Saba will bring gifts, those coming toward the evening of the faulty life, so that the light of the impious might be darkened by them. And it is possible for one to be falsely transformed into an angel of light until he deceives even the elect; for Arabs are interpreted as morning and evening. After these Arabs and many others, repentance is offered by Saba; and the name is taken for the return.

It is possible to take as those worshiping him and offering gifts the teachers of all the nations, the apostles and disciples and the successors of these; for they offer gifts to God from the men who are profited by them. And if even one of the faithful brings gifts of praiseworthy deeds and true mindset, it is as if kings bring their own gifts to the only and one All-King. It is also written that his name is honored, having delivered them from so many evils (Ps 72:14). Having learned, the holy men, that no one of the born [humanity] will deliver men from the prevailing wickedness, all turned away and were made blameless concerning the [unclear]...

Wishing to be saved from the hand of the powerful and becoming a cause of eternal salvation, they were continually and unceasingly sending prayer to the Father, at times saying, 'Show us, Lord, your mercy and grant us your salvation,' and at other times, 'Send out your light and your truth.' Concerning his sending and at the beginning of the present Psalm 71, they prayed saying, 'O God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king' (Ps 71:15c).

They glorify him through all the days of this present age or of the enlightened life of those blessing (Ps 71:16a). The outcomes of the anticipatory proclamations are more extreme than these mountains, for the one prophesied has become a support in the land (Ps 71:16a).

For Jesus did not bear fruit through the arrival of faithful men, and they possess a multitude and greatness of deeds and theorems; but a witness to this is [the promise] that 'the righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, and like a cedar in Lebanon he shall multiply' (Ps 71:16bc). For when the fruit of the support has been multiplied and exceeded, the Jews who were unfaithful to the Savior shall spring up from the city of Jerusalem like grass from the earth, because of the parched state and the rapid drying up, so named and most justly.

Since they have become flesh in their wisdom, having been unfaithful to the Savior and seeking glory from one another rather than that which is given by God alone, they shall spring up from the earth as grass; for all flesh is grass and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass. For they shall not merely bloom, but shall spring up [and wither].

And also those of the grass, whether out of the city or not in the city, shall spring up, those of whom the word is. For those who hastened toward life and wisdom outside the spiritual city, Jerusalem, were dried up like the parched and rapidly drying grass; but of the one remaining within the city, nothing of this sort was experienced; for 'he who dwells in Jerusalem shall never be shaken' (Ps 71:17c–19a).

The nations, which are to be blessed in him, make happy the one who blessed them, saying, 'Blessed is the Lord, the God of the discerning race, who alone has done wondrous things, having freed us from idolatry and the treatment of wandering demons; for truly it is a wonder.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
